label: At D2, update gate drops after choosing a1 / believing S1 good, growing late in episode.
short_terms: (phase == D2) * belief * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo * ep_trial
terms: (phase == D2) * belief_lo * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_action == 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_state == 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1)
explanation: Raw z of unit 11 is ~1 at D1/GO (tiny residuals) and dips at D2, increasingly so later in the episode (timing). Beyond timing, the D2 value is lower when the just-made choice is a1 (and slightly when S1 is reached) and when the ideal observer believes S1 is good (belief_lo), higher for a2 / S2-good beliefs; the effect scales with episode time (ep_dec), matching the growing D2 dip. All terms are observed at D2. The free fit adds the previous trial choice/state and a1-S2-rewarded / a2-rewarded history at D2 and unscaled versions (dev 0.70 vs 0.65). Residual misses come from saturation near 1 (a2/S2 cases under-predicted) and small late-episode D1/GO dips not modelled.

issues: The state term does nothing. Without (phase==D2)*(state==1)*ep_dec the test R^2 is 0.6469, against 0.6473 with it, and its fitted weight is only -0.002. So the claim that it is 'a little lower when S1 is reached' adds nothing beyond the choice and belief.

Scaling by ep_dec is weaker than scaling by ep_trial. The same three terms score 0.660 on test with ep_trial versus 0.647 with ep_dec. The D2 timing dip speeds up late in the episode (0.92 -> 0.55 -> 0.25 over the last deciles), so a step function of decile is a poor multiplier.

Running misses on the recorded short form shows a large systematic error class, not scattered noise. At D2 it under-predicts after S2-favouring histories: after a2 S2 u by +0.105, after a1 S2 r by +0.097, after a2 S1 r by +0.076. Worst-case windows late in the episode with confident S2 belief have an actual D2 z of about 0.8-0.9 where the prediction is 0.36-0.49. The cause is saturation: a linear belief_lo term cannot hold z near 1 for strong S2 belief while also giving the deep dip for S1.
Misses also shows phase-mean bias under the recorded form: D1 -0.009, GO -0.009, D2 +0.019. This disappears (to about 0.001-0.002) with the better form below.

The directions in the label are right. At D2, z is lower after choosing a1 and when belief favours S1 (belief-decile residuals go from +0.146 to -0.19), and these effects grow with episode time. Effects at D1 and GO are about 0.005 and negligible. No future variables are used.

Better short form, which passes --short: (phase == D2) * belief * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * ep_trial ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo * ep_trial. Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.740 (dev 0.737), close to the 0.76 additive ceiling. It shrinks the worst D2 under-prediction from +0.105 to +0.071 (after a1 S2 r), and after a2 S2 u from +0.105 to +0.041. One caveat: belief (+) and belief_lo (-) get opposite-sign weights. Together they make a saturating shape: flat at moderate beliefs, and strongly driven only at confident beliefs. It is a shape correction, though an interpretable one.
